title: claire wong - SRE oncall scratchpad 2026-03-25
content:
Date: 2026-03-25
Shift: 09:00 - 17:00 PT (handoff from noah at 09:00)

Summary / TL;DR:
- Handled 1 Sev-2 latency incident (IR-2026-03-25-01). Backend autoscaling underprovisioned during traffic burst; observed queue length spike and GC churn on a subset of inference workers. Rolled back a recent scaling policy change & temporarily increased pool size to stabilize.
- Follow-ups listed below (runbook updates, alert tuning, postmortem).

Incidents / Pages:
1) IR-2026-03-25-01 — API latency spike (page at 09:17)
   - Trigger: p95 token generation latency > 2.5s for > 3m, error budget warning fired.
   - Initial detection: synthetic monitor alerted (eu-west-1 region) + customer ticket complaining about slow chat responses.
   - Timeline:
     * 09:17 — Pager (severity 2) to oncall.
     * 09:20 — Slack: started triage in #sre-oncall. Quick grep of metrics: CPU load and queue length on warm pools increased on worker-group g4dn-1-critical.
     * 09:26 — Checked autoscaler history: a rollout yesterday changed the scale-down threshold from 60s -> 30s. Suspect aggressive scale-down causing underprovision during burst. Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-987 (autoscaler rollout PR).
     * 09:30 — Scaled dedicated pool up by +30% (manual override) to mitigate. Deployed temporary override via infra control-plane.
     * 09:36 — Latency p95 returning to baseline.
     * 09:50 — Verified with synthetic: stable for 15m; escalated to customer success for communication.
   - Mitigation performed:
     * Reverted scale-down threshold to 60s on g4dn-1-critical group (rollback of yesterday's change).
     * Manually increased min replica count for the group to handle bursts until autoscaler fix is validated.
   - Root cause (initial hypothesis): rolling out a more aggressive scale-down threshold (30s) caused instances to terminate too fast during short bursts, combined with slightly higher-than-normal GC pauses on a subset of workers. Leads to queueing and head-of-line latency.
   - Evidence to collect:
     * gc logs from g4dn-1-critical workers (09:00-10:00).
     * autoscaler controller logs for the rollout window.
     * synthetic monitor traces for correlation.
   - Owners:
     * immediate mitigation: claire wong (me)
     * autoscaler change review + fix: infra team (owner: lena garcia) -- see INF-987
     * GC investigation: serving-runtime team (owner: noah chen)

Action items / Follow-ups (short-term):
- [ ] Create SRE postmortem stub in Confluence and attach logs (owner: claire, due: 2026-03-27) -- use template under /pages/api-latency-postmortem.
- [ ] Add an alert that correlates scale events with p95 latency (owner: lena, due: 2026-03-26).
- [ ] Add a guard in autoscaler rollout PRs to block threshold changes without canary (owner: infra, due: 2026-04-02) -- linked INF-987.
- [ ] Pull GC traces and heap profiles, hand to serving-runtime (owner: claire -> noah, due: 2026-03-26).
- [ ] Re-run load tests with scale-down=30s in staging and validate behavior (owner: load-testing team, requested by: claire).
- [ ] Update customer-facing status update (CS pinged at 10:05) and confirm closure (owner: customer-success).

Runbook TODOs / Notes to update:
- api-latency-runbook (Confluence)
  - Missing: explicit steps to rollback autoscaler config + how to apply temporary min-replica override. Add CLI commands and UI screenshots.
  - Add a troubleshooting checklist: "If p95 > X and scale events > Y in last 5m -> check autoscaler history".
  - Add runbook snippet for GC diagnosis (where to find heap dumps, how to symbolicate, who to page).
  - Add playbook to coordinate with CS for customer comms.

Triage notes / debug commands used (short snippets):
- qlen summary: kubectl top pods -n inference --selector=worker-group=g4dn-1-critical && ./metrics-queries/p95_latency.sh --range 1h --region eu-west-1
- autoscaler history: curl https://infra-api.redwood.internal/autoscaler/history?group=g4dn-1-critical | jq '.events | .[] | {time,action,replicas}'
- gc logs location: s3://redwood-logs/prod/g4dn-1-critical/gc/2026-03-25/*.log

Notes to self (oncall tips):
- Don't forget to bump min replicas before removing temporary override.
- If rolling back autoscaler configs, leave a 1h window to observe before marking incident resolved.
- Add a short blameless note in postmortem about config drift and insufficient canarying.

Other items during shift:
- 11:40 — Noticed slightly elevated 5xx for embeddings endpoint in us-west-2 (spike to 0.9% for ~8m). Investigated quickly: transient DB connection errors from metadata-store pool exhaustion. Temporarily increased pool size and added backpressure. Ticket SRE-452 created for DB pool tuning. (owner: david choi).
- 13:30 — Attended 30m sync with infra about model rollout policies. Flagged need for pre-rollout canaries for scaler changes.

Meeting / Handoff notes for next oncall (sophia):
- Main items open: postmortem stub (confluence), GC logs pulled but not analyzed, INF-987 needs a follow-up PR that adds canary guard.
- TODOs that you can pick up: add alert correlation (lena owns but could use help), follow up with serving-runtime on heap dump analysis.
- Slack breadcrumbs: #sre-oncall thread ts:1623456789 (link in linked_artifacts).

Unresolved questions / Risks:
- Are some worker types more susceptible to GC pauses due to model memory layout? (serving-runtime to investigate)
- Does the autoscaler metric resolution (30s vs 60s) cause oscillation under frequent small bursts? Need a staging experiment.

Personal TODOs (post-shift):
- [ ] Draft postmortem intro + timeline (30-45m)
- [ ] Add runbook steps for manual override (15m)
- [ ] Follow up with lena to confirm alert query changes (quick sync)

Quick reminders / scratchpad lines:
- Keep an eye on EU synthetic monitors for next 6 hours.
- Note: customer "Acme AI" reported ~10% slower response; CS tracking.
- Remember to archive incident logs to S3 path and attach to Confluence.

Random notes / fragments (for search):
- "scale-down threshold rollback helped stabilize p95"
- "consider heartbeat metric for worker liveness or prefetch kv-cache"
- "maybe add small buffer to GC heap config for g4dn families"

End of shift handoff at 17:00.
